actions.action: Do a soil test before planting
Work fertilizer or up to one inch of compost into the top six inches of soil
Sow seeds 1/8 inch deep or plant transplants after last frost
Thin seedlings to 3-4 inches, then to about 12 inches apart
Water about 1.5 inches per week, keeping soil consistently moist
Feed with liquid nitrogen fertilizer such as fish emulsion (weekly for containers)
Lay organic mulch around young plants
Cover young plants with row cover against pests
Harvest leaf stems once plant has 6-8 leaves, leaving 2-4 leaves
Stagger basil plantings every other week
Plant extra basil to let flower for pollinators
Watch the linked YouTube video on basil varieties
Prepare a raised bed or amend ground soil with rich organic mix
Cut back the flowering top portion of the plant, then fertilize and keep moist

verdict.reason: The answer is a generic basil-growing article that never identifies the plant as healthy and just needing bushier growth; cutting back flowers and fertilizing appears only buried and contradicted by a claim that pinching doesn't help, repotting into a bigger pot is absent, and nothing is clearly likely to harm the plant.
